title: fleet.task.v1
description: A unit of work the orchestrator can hand to one agent: one repo, one branch, one worktree (docs/agent-fleet.md principle 5). Everything an agent is permitted to touch and everything the orchestrator will check afterwards is declared here, up front, rather than discovered from the agent's own narration (docs/fleet.md).

id.description: Unique task identifier, e.g. 'R2.11', 'CI-4', 'ROOT-DOC-1'. Unique across fleet/tasks/ (checked by fleet.py validate, not by this schema alone, since uniqueness is a cross-file property).

title.description: One-line human-readable summary of the task.

repo.description: Which repo the agent runs in: the workspace root, or one of the two service submodules (AGENTS.md repo map). An agent assigned here edits only that repo (AGENTS.md section 3).

base.description: Branch this task's branch is created from. Defaults to 'main' when omitted; fleet.py applies the default, the schema only documents it.

branch.description: Branch name the agent commits to, inside its own worktree (AGENTS.md section 5: one agent = one worktree = one branch).

needs.description: Dependencies that must hold before this task can start. A need whose 'task' does not match any id in fleet/tasks/ is treated as an explicit external marker (historical work merged before the fleet existed, e.g. 'R2.9') and is trusted at face value only when its state is 'merged' -- fleet.py has no record to verify an external 'pushed' claim against.

allowed_paths.description: Glob patterns, relative to this task's repo root, naming every path the agent may create or modify. The orchestrator diffs the agent's commits against this list after the run (allowed_paths_violations in result.v1.json); fleet.py plan additionally checks that same-repo, same-layer tasks do not claim overlapping globs.

acceptance.description: Commands the orchestrator itself runs after the agent hands back control -- never the agent's own say-so (docs/fleet.md: agents are untrusted narrators).

prompt_file.description: Path, relative to the workspace root, to this task's prompt (fleet/prompts/<id>.md). fleet.py validate checks the file exists.

model.description: Model identifier or capability tier (docs/agent-fleet.md section 2) the agent runs on.

max_turns.description: Hard cap on agent turns for this task, enforced by the orchestrator, not the agent.

risk.description: Coarse blast-radius classification used to decide review depth and serialization caution. 'docs' = prose only, 'ci' = pipeline/workflow config, 'code' = application source.

task.description: Id of the task this depends on, or an external marker id not present in fleet/tasks/.

state.description: 'pushed' = the dependency's branch has been pushed by the orchestrator (not yet merged); 'merged' = it has landed on its base branch.

safeGlob.description: A relative glob/path: no leading '/' or '\\', no drive letter, and no '..' path segment anywhere (start, middle, or end). Keeps every declared path inside the repo it names.

name.description: Short label for this check, shown in result.v1.json acceptance_results.

cwd.description: Directory the command runs in, relative to the task's repo root ('.' for the repo root itself).

command.description: Shell command the orchestrator runs verbatim. Never the agent.

expect_exit.description: Exit code that counts as a pass for this check.
